case.pattern_description: A coordinated multi-card fraud syndicate utilizes a specific device profile (Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge SM-G935F) routed through an anonymous proxy to execute unauthorized online transactions across dozens of unrelated card accounts. The transactions are deliberately structured to evade automated fraud detection models, which assign low risk scores despite the high volume of linked accounts. The syndicate systematically targets cards with predominantly in-person retail baselines.

evidence.claim: Automated fraud model assigned transaction 3468314 a low model score of 0.006 with a historical fraud rate of 0.006, and legacy risk score of 0.01.
Transaction 3468314 was conducted within region 126, consistent with 63 of the 65 historical transactions on card C02910-K1.

Card C02910-K1 has an established baseline heavily dominated by in-person retail purchases in product category W (60 of 65 prior txns), making this online transaction 3468314 in product category C an abrupt behavioral departure.
Transaction 3468314 originated from device D004630, which was newly introduced to card C02910-K1 and operated behind an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).

Device D004630 connects card C02910-K1 to fraud ring 36700632 and has been actively used across 18 distinct cards in the 30-day monitoring window, appearing as a new device behind an anonymous proxy on each account.

Device D004630 is directly tied to four confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, CC-3035) exhibiting an undocumented multi-card typology, and card C02910-K1 itself suffered three prior confirmed-fraud cases (CC-4131, CC-4752, CC-5256).

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: Monitoring alert MON-017 flagged online transaction 3468314 ($224.80) on card C02910-K1 due to graph linkage with fraud ring 36700632. The transaction originated from device D004630 (Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge SM-G935F) operating behind an anonymous proxy, which was newly introduced across 18 distinct cards in a 30-day window and is tied to four confirmed fraud cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035). Although automated models assigned a low risk score of 0.006, the transaction sharply deviates from the cardholder's normal in-person retail purchasing baseline. The case was assessed as an undocumented multi-card syndicate pattern, resulting in case creation, regulatory reporting, and connected card monitoring.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details suspected coordinated card fraud identified on card C02910-K1 under customer bucket C02910. On November 18, 2016, at 18:17:00 UTC, an unauthorized online transaction 3468314 totaling $224.80 in product category C was processed in region 126. The transaction originated from device D004630, identified as a Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M, Android 7.0, Chrome 62.0), operating behind an anonymous proxy service. Device D004630 was newly registered to card C02910-K1 and links directly to connected-component fraud ring 36700632. Graph analysis revealed that device D004630 was utilized across 18 distinct cards within a 30-day window, appearing as a new device behind an anonymous proxy on each account. The shared device links card C02910-K1 to 17 other active cards, including C09906-K1, C01996-K2, and C04108-K2. Furthermore, device D004630 is directly tied to four prior confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035) exhibiting an undocumented multi-card syndicate pattern. Card C02910-K1 previously sustained confirmed fraud compromises under cases CC-4131, CC-4752, and CC-5256. The online category C transaction sharply deviates from the cardholder's established history of 60 in-person retail purchases in category W. The total exposure identified in this alert is $224.80, with related syndicate activity placed under ongoing monitoring.

stop_reason: Investigation concluded pursuant to policy section 6 because decisive cross-card graph evidence and prior confirmed fraud links firmly established an undocumented multi-card syndicate, reaching an actionable probability where further inquiry would not alter the required escalation and filing actions.
